la:noun:anhelitus.html:
ănhēlĭtus, ūs, m.
id.
.
A difficulty of breathing, panting, puffing (class. for the post-Aug. anhelatio): ex cursurā anhelitum ducere,to pant,: nimiae celeritates gressus cum fiunt, anhelitus moventur,quickness of breathing is caused,: anhelitum vix sufferre,: anhelitum recipere,: sublimis anhelitus, deep, * : creber,quick,: vastos quatit aeger anhelitus artus,painful panting,: aridus e lasso veniebat anhelitus ore,; ; .—As a disease, the asthma (cf. anhelatio), .—
In gen., breathing, breath: unguentorum odor, vini anhelitus,breath smelling of wine,: male odorati anhelitus oris,bad breath,: anhelitum reddere ac per vices recipere,to breathe out and in,—
Metaph., of other things, breath, exhalation, vapor: credo etiam anhelitus quosdam fuisse terrarum, quibus inflatae mentes oracula funderent,: placet Stoicos eos anhelitus terrae, qui frigidi sunt, cum fluere coeperint, ventos esse,.

la:verb:anhelo.gloss: to breathe out, breathe forth, exhale
senses: to breathe out, breathe forth, exhale
to draw the breath with difficulty, pant, puff, gasp
to emit vapour, puff; roar, crash
la:verb:anhelo.html:
ănhēlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[2. anand halo].
Verb. neutr.
Pr., to move about for breath; hence, to draw the breath with great difficulty, to pant, puff, gasp, etc.: anhelat inconstanter,: cum languida anhelant,: * : anhelans ex imis pulmonibus prae curā spiritus ducebatur, Auct. ad : anhelans Colla fovet,; : nullus anhelabat sub adunco vomere taurus,: sudare atque anhelare,.— In gen., to breathe (cf. anhelitus, II.), .—
Metaph., of fire: fornacibus ignis anhelat,roars,.—Of the earth: subter anhelat humus,heaves,.—Of the foaming of the sea, .—Trop., of poverty panting for something: anhelans inopia,.—
Verb. act., to breathe out, to emit by breathing, breathe forth, exhale: nolo verba exiliter exanimata exire, nolo inflata et quasi anhelata gravius,: de pectore frigus anhelans Capricornus, vet. poët. ap. : anhelati ignes,; so : rabiem anhelare,: anhelatis exsurgens ictibus alnus,the strokes of the oars made with panting,.—Trop., to pursue, pant for, strive after something with eagerness: Catilinam furentem audaciā, scelus anhelantem,breathing out wickedness,: anhelans ex imo pectore crudelitatem, Auct. ad .!*? Some, as Corssen, Ausspr. II. p. 564, regard the prefix of this word as the Gr. ἀνά; hence, pr. to draw up the breath; cf. antestor.
